descriptions.text: Tangaroa and Rongo are the twin sons of Vatea and Papa. Gill distinguishes Tangaroa’s seniority by right from Rongo’s earlier birth. Tangaroa teaches agriculture and receives red produce and fish; Papa secures precedence for Rongo. Tangaroa departs for Rarotonga and Aitutaki. On Mangaia, Gill records coconut buds offered at his little-used marae.

sources.reference: William Wyatt Gill, Myths and Songs from the South Pacific (1876), pp. 10–14, 19

variants.description: Gill records two accounts: Tangaroa emerges from a boil on Papa’s arm, or through her head. Neither changes the named parents.
